title: Two tower proposals and active transportation progress
subtitle: Library public artwork, Wellington Street infill housing, tax and utility write-offs, and a push for more density on Charles Street
overview: The committee recommended approving a 25-storey mixed-use tower at 130-142 Victoria Street South and a 17-storey tower at 332 Charles Street East. For Charles Street, it added a direction for staff to explore extra density in return for community benefits such as affordability or environmental measures. Staff are to report back to Council on September 25. It also recommended approving 13 new units behind an existing duplex at 229 Wellington Street North.

The committee received the first progress report on the Cycling and Trails Master Plan. Staff said 24 of 35 actions have been achieved. Delegates mostly praised the progress, while one raised concerns about the one-way conversion of Joseph Street. Staff said a safety study will include emergency services and traffic volumes.

Other recommendations include a Indigenous-created public artwork for the new southwest library, lifting holding provisions on two sites, and write-offs of uncollectable accounts and tax adjustments. These go to Council for final decisions.
Residents will see how intensification, parking reductions, rental displacement and cycling routes are being handled.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting an Official Plan amendment, approving rezoning for a 25-storey mixed-use development, and endorsing its development concept {{vote:m9}}.
The committee recommended a 17-storey mixed-use development and, as amended, directed staff to explore additional density with community benefits and report to Council on September 25 {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended rezoning to allow a three-storey rear addition with 13 units behind the existing duplex {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended commissioning "Wintertime Stories" for the new Kitchener Public Library southwest facility and authorizing an artist agreement {{vote:m6}}.
The committee received the first progress report on the Cycling and Trails Master Plan for information {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended approving applications for write-off, cancellation, reduction or refund of taxes totalling $656,395.31 {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended writing off $109,658 in uncollectable utility accounts {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended lifting Holding Provision 43H from the site {{vote:m5}}.

debate: On Charles Street, one councillor argued this was a one-time chance to secure more housing near transit. Another opposed the amendment, saying adequate community benefit is hard to define and that affordability at 80% of market value does not address the crisis.

On cycling, most delegates described safer, more useful routes and asked for better connections near schools, more trail signage and consistent crossings. One delegate opposed the one-way Joseph Street conversion, citing emergency access, longer trips and doubts about the cyclist counts.

Staff said emergency services were consulted on the Joseph Street design and that a third-party safety study will interview emergency services. They said traffic volumes on the street have dropped sharply.

On Wellington Street, a delegate objected to the low parking rate. One councillor replied that parking adds housing costs and the city has underused garages. The applicant's consultant said keeping the existing building preserves neighbourhood character.

On Victoria Street, councillors raised concerns about displacement of 12 month-to-month tenants. They also asked about the heritage building's demolition, dog space, sustainability and the very small number of parking spaces.
